title: Unsafe Pointer Escape and Buffer Bounds
platform_conditions: Swift runtime language semantics (Unsafe pointer family); applies wherever Swift runs (iOS/macOS and server-side Swift on Linux)
security_mechanism: withUnsafeBytes/withUnsafeMutableBytes hand the closure a pointer that is only valid for the duration of the call: the buffer's backing storage can be reallocated or freed the moment the closure returns, so storing the pointer in an outer variable and dereferencing it later is use-after-free by construction, not just a style warning. bindMemory and assumingMemoryBound reinterpret raw bytes as a typed T; if the real bytes were attacker-influenced or the alignment/stride assumption is wrong, reads return type-confused values and writes corrupt unrelated memory. Unmanaged retains the pre-ARC calling convention: a mismatched retain/release pair (retain().release() vs toOpaque()/fromOpaque()) produces a leak or a double release that attackers can groom.

source_sink_clues.source: External data whose length or content determines the buffer's lifetime or interpretation: network packets, parsed files, IPC messages fed into pointer-based processing.
source_sink_clues.sink: withUnsafeBytes { ptr = $0.baseAddress } and any escape of the closure-scoped pointer; bindMemory / assumingMemoryBound on externally sized raw buffers; UnsafeMutablePointer / UnsafeRawBufferPointer arithmetic with input-derived offsets; Unmanaged retain/release imbalance

tracking_guards: Check every unsafe pointer is consumed inside its with* closure (no assignment to outer scope, no stored baseAddress); check lengths used for pointer arithmetic or bindMemory counts are validated against the real allocation size before use; check Unmanaged pairs are balanced (or takeRetainedValue/takeUnretainedValue used correctly) at every path.
not_candidate_when: The pointer is used only within the withUnsafeBytes closure on a buffer sized from compile-time constants, the reinterpretation is on internal fixed-layout structs never fed by external bytes, or the value is fully bridged through safe Swift collections before any use outside the closure.
public_references: CWE-119: Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/119.html
Swift Programming Language guide: Unsafe Pointer (Memory Safety chapter)
